questions.key_step: Assertion-reason on a 3x3 system: Delta=0, then decide consistency from one determinant.
questions.justification: Routine two-step chain (evaluate Delta, evaluate the constants determinant, link them); no insight beyond Cramer's rule criterion. Close to 2023-P1-Q14 but with one system and no parameters.

questions.key_step: Eliminate xyz sin3θ between the equations to reach y+z=0, x=0, tan3θ=1 and count roots; reject sin3θ=0.
questions.justification: Needs a non-obvious elimination of a common expression, then a case check and a root count with no options; one slip changes the integer. Level 3 as a single short chain.

questions.key_step: Row and column differences make the determinant triangular, giving -8α^3.
questions.justification: Two rounds of operations on squared entries then a cubic; options let a student check, but sign care is needed and the 3x3 of squares is less familiar than plain ones.

questions.key_step: Split the third column; both pieces are Vandermonde-type.
questions.justification: Splitting by linearity plus the (a-b)(b-c)(c-a) lemma plus a quadratic in x^3 and counting real cube roots; numerical answer, no options.

questions.key_step: Compare ratios a/3, 2/(-2), λ/μ for four statements.
questions.justification: Four short statements on a 2x2 system, each a one-line check with the standard ratio test; one concept only, so no multi-concept floor.

questions.key_step: Reciprocals in AP make the third equation a combination of the first two, so consistency means a=d.
questions.justification: HP to AP conversion, four conditions, matching with a solution check; the dependency of the third equation is non-obvious and Cramer's route is long.

questions.key_step: D=7α-2β-3, then check D_z for γ and use y=-2 when α=1.
questions.justification: Same style and length as 2023-P1-Q14 (which is rated L3): unique / none / infinite / particular solution matching with parameters.
